_comment: Declared relation-level equivalences used to normalise claims before matching. DESIGN COMMITMENT: canonicalization is done by explicit, auditable rules, not by a similarity threshold. The reason is that this project's hardest safety gate is the false-merge rate, and a threshold gives no account of WHY two claims were merged. With declared rules, every merge traces to a named rule and a bad merge is a bug in a specific rule that can be removed, rather than a number that has to be retuned and hoped about. Adding a rule is a deliberate act and must carry a justification.

relation_equivalences.justification: To say agents act synergistically for an outcome IS to say their combination outperforms the single agents. Definitional, not empirical. Verified against both source papers: Carlisle 2012 reports 'no synergism between antiemetics', and Fujii's 2002 review states the same claim as a combination being 'more effective than one drug alone'. Two relations, one claim.
relation_equivalences.guard_rationale: Without the guard this rule over-applies. MORE_EFFECTIVE_THAN is also used for plain drug-versus-drug comparisons (granisetron beats droperidol), which have nothing to do with synergy, and normalising those onto COMBINATION_OUTPERFORMS would make them look related to the synergy claim. The rule therefore fires only when the superior term actually denotes a combination. Caught by reasoning through the decoy pairs before running, not after.
relation_equivalences.added_because: eval/canonicalization_eval.py measured F1 0.000 with no matcher able to see this real cross-document duplicate.

role_aliases._comment: Per-relation role-name synonyms, applied after symbol alignment. EARNED, not prophylactic: an earlier review flagged that argument roles are unregistered free strings and two compilers could emit different names for one role, and I deferred it as speculative. The first end-to-end run then produced exactly that failure. The blind extraction encoded granisetron-beats-droperidol with roles agent/comparator while the reference used better/worse, so two identical claims compared as DIFFERENT purely on role naming. Only genuine synonyms are listed: a role pair that means something different must NOT be aliased, because that is a false merge wearing a rename.

symbol_families._comment: Declared outcome families, used when aligning two independently invented vocabularies. Implements EXTRACTION_SPEC.md rule 2a at the symbol level: separate endpoints of one outcome family collapse to the family, because the same trials support all of them and they are not independently retractable. Needed because the blind extraction emitted three endpoint symbols (postoperative nausea, postoperative vomiting, postoperative nausea or vomiting) where the reference graph has one. Declared rather than inferred from label substrings, since 'nausea' being a substring of 'nausea or vomiting' is a coincidence of English, not evidence about endpoints.

non_discriminating_roles._comment: Roles that may be absent from one graph without blocking a match, because they restate a constant of the corpus rather than distinguishing claims. 'population' qualifies here ONLY because every claim in this corpus is about the same surgical-prophylaxis population; in a corpus spanning populations it would be discriminating and dropping it would be a false merge. Recorded with that caveat so the exemption is not silently carried into a corpus where it is wrong.

symbol_denotations._comment: Declared properties of symbols that rule guards test. Kept explicit and small rather than inferred from labels, because a guard that silently mis-fires reintroduces exactly the false merges the rules exist to prevent.

notes.scope: One rule. Deliberately. A rule is added only when a measured matching failure demands it, on the same discipline as the K-IR schema changes: earned, not designed upfront. A file of speculative equivalences would be the Cyc trap in miniature.
notes.what_normalisation_does_not_do: It maps relations onto a shared canonical predicate and reorders roles. It does NOT weaken arguments, so a specific instance never normalises onto the general principle it instantiates. That distinction is handled separately as subsumption, and reporting subsumption as equality is exactly the false merge the gate forbids.
